instances.scene: Harry stood in the damp, deserted bathroom, listening to Moaning Myrtle's sobbing account of her death. 'I just saw a pair of great, big, yellow eyes,' she wailed, 'and then I died!'
instances.event: Harry, after learning how Myrtle died, is asked about a future event where he will open a golden egg underwater and hear a merpeople's song.
instances.summary: The question is set immediately after the event where Moaning Myrtle reveals the cause of her death, and asks about an event that will occur much later.
instances.question: Harry, right after hearing Myrtle explain how she saw the yellow eyes and died, Ron mentions he's heard a rumour about a magical egg that might reveal secrets underwater one day. What would you say to him about that?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set immediately after the event where Moaning Myrtle reveals the cause of her death, and asks about an event that will occur much later.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom
instances.Gold_Response:
If there’s a magical egg that tells you things underwater, Ron, I’d rather it told us how to stop people being Petrified than anything else.  

But honestly, after hearing Myrtle talk about those eyes, I’d trust a great bloody egg a lot more than going swimming in the same place that thing’s been lurking. If we ever find one, you can be the one to test it in the bath.

instances.scene: In the small, cramped sitting room of the cottage, Ron turned to Harry, his brow furrowed with concern. 'I don't know, Harry,' he said, his voice low. 'Chasing the Hallows... it just feels wrong. We should be focusing on the Horcruxes.'
instances.event: Ron expresses his doubts to Harry about the decision to pursue the Deathly Hallows instead of focusing solely on the Horcruxes.
instances.summary: The question is set immediately after Ron expressed his doubts about the Hallows, which occurs before the trio's meeting with Griphook and their eventual escape from Gringotts on a dragon.
instances.question: Harry, right after Ron voiced his concerns about your focus on the Hallows, Hermione mentions she's worried that breaking into Gringotts might involve a dragon guarding the vaults. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set immediately after Ron expressed his doubts about the Hallows, which occurs before the trio's meeting with Griphook and their eventual escape from Gringotts on a dragon.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 25, whenever they were together in the first few days
instances.Gold_Response:
It’s bloody terrifying, if I’m honest. I’ve seen a dragon up close before, and it was bad enough when all I had to do was grab an egg and get out, never mind sneaking round one in a vault underground.

But if there *is* a dragon down there, then it’s just one more thing we’ve got to get past. Voldemort’s still worse than any dragon, and if there’s a Horcrux in that vault, we don’t really have a choice. I’m not going to turn back because of a “maybe” dragon. We’ll figure something out when we have to – we always do.

instances.scene: On the bustling platform nine and three-quarters, just before the Hogwarts Express was due to depart, Harry pulled Mr. Weasley aside. 'I think Draco Malfoy's a Death Eater,' Harry muttered, his voice low and urgent.
instances.event: At King's Cross station before the start of the school term, Harry confides in Arthur Weasley, sharing his strong suspicion that Draco Malfoy has become a Death Eater.
instances.summary: The question concerns events that occur after Harry shares his initial suspicion about Malfoy on the platform.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told Mr. Weasley about your suspicions regarding Malfoy on the platform, he asks you: 'What do you think Malfoy's specific mission for Voldemort will be, and how will it play out this year?' What is your response?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question concerns events that occur after Harry shares his initial suspicion about Malfoy on the platform.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 7, at platform before train departure

instances.scene: The high voice spoke from the back of Quirrell's head. 'See what I have become?' it said. 'Mere shadow and vapour... only when I can have another body will I be able to touch the Stone...'
instances.event: Voldemort explains his current spectral state and his desperate need for the Philosopher's Stone to regain a proper body.
instances.summary: Knowledge state of Harry Potter immediately after learning the full extent of Voldemort's current physical limitations and goals.
instances.question: Harry, immediately after Voldemort explains his spectral form and need for the Stone, you are asked if he will succeed in getting a new body. What is your response?
instances.Spatio_Label: Knowledge state of Harry Potter immediately after learning the full extent of Voldemort's current physical limitations and goals.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, after demanding to speak to Harry face-to-face

instances.scene: In Dumbledore's office, after the events in the Chamber of Secrets, Harry sat before the headmaster. 'You can speak Parseltongue, Harry,' said Dumbledore calmly, 'because Lord Voldemort transferred some of his own powers to you the night he gave you that scar.'
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry that his ability to speak Parseltongue is a result of Voldemort transferring some of his powers to Harry on the night of the attack.
instances.summary: Immediately following Dumbledore's revelation about the origin of Harry's Parseltongue ability
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore told you that Voldemort's powers were transferred to you through your scar, Ron mentioned he's worried that this connection might mean Voldemort could plant false visions in your mind someday. What would you say to him?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately following Dumbledore's revelation about the origin of Harry's Parseltongue ability
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, during private conversation
instances.Gold_Response:
If You-Know-Who could do that, I reckon he would’ve tried already, especially this year with everything that’s happened. My scar hurts when he’s close, or when something to do with him is happening, but that’s not the same as him being inside my head, telling me what to see.

And even if there is some sort of… link, it doesn’t make me him. The Sorting Hat wanted to put me in Slytherin, but I chose not to. Fawkes came to me because I stayed loyal to Dumbledore, and I pulled the sword of Gryffindor out of that hat. All that has to mean something.

Maybe there is a bit of You-Know-Who in me, like Dumbledore said, but I know who I am. If he ever tried to shove anything into my mind, I’d fight it. And if anything ever started feeling wrong in my head, you and Hermione would be the first to know. I’m not going to just sit there and let him use me.

instances.scene: The door to the Ravenclaw common room swung shut behind them. Luna, looking around the deserted room, spoke thoughtfully. 'You know, if there's a real fight later, I hope we'll have enough people who can cast Patronuses if the Dementors come.'
instances.event: Inside the Ravenclaw common room, Luna speculates about the potential need for multiple Patronus casters during a future confrontation.
instances.summary: During the initial search of the Ravenclaw common room, long before the nighttime battle where Luna, Ernie, and Seamus help fight Dementors.
instances.question: Harry, back when we were first searching the Ravenclaw common room for the diadem, Luna wondered if we'd have enough people to fight off Dementors with Patronuses if a big battle broke out. How do you see that situation playing out?
instances.Spatio_Label: During the initial search of the Ravenclaw common room, long before the nighttime battle where Luna, Ernie, and Seamus help fight Dementors.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 29, at the Ravenclaw common room entrance
instances.Gold_Response:
If it came to that here at Hogwarts, with Dementors swarming in and a real fight breaking out, it’d be rough, no point pretending otherwise. There aren’t many of us who can cast a proper Patronus, and most people have had the hope sucked out of them all year by the Carrows and Snape. That makes it harder.

But if there *was* a battle, it would mean people had finally decided they’d had enough, and that changes things. Once people see Dementors driven back – once they see they *can* be fought – more of them will find something inside themselves to hold on to. Luna, me, a few of the DA, maybe some of the teachers, we’d have to hold the line at first, keep the Dementors off everyone else until they could get their heads clear and fight. It wouldn’t be neat or easy, and some people would probably break, but I don’t believe Dementors could stand up forever against a castle full of people who’ve decided they’re done being frightened.

instances.scene: Scrimgeour led Harry out into the snowy garden, away from the Burrow's Christmas lunch. 'I thought we might take a brief stroll,' the Minister said, his lion-like mane dusted with snow.
instances.event: Minister Scrimgeour takes Harry Potter into the garden for a private conversation shortly after arriving at the Burrow on Christmas.
instances.summary: Immediately after Scrimgeour separates Harry from the Christmas gathering for their private garden conversation
instances.question: Harry, right after Scrimgeour pulled you aside into the garden, Ron mentioned he's afraid the Ministry might start interfering at Hogwarts again. What do you think will happen?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after Scrimgeour separates Harry from the Christmas gathering for their private garden conversation
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 16, Shortly after Percy's arrival on Christmas
instances.Gold_Response:
Wouldn’t put it past them to try.

Fudge stuck his nose in last year and it was a complete disaster, and Scrimgeour doesn’t feel all that different so far, just a bit tougher and sneakier. If they start meddling again, it’ll be to make themselves look like they’re doing something about Voldemort, not because they actually care what happens to us.

But Dumbledore’s back in charge and that makes it a lot harder for them to shove some Umbridge-type into the castle again. If they do try anything, I’ll back Dumbledore, not the Ministry, and they can say whatever they like about me in the Prophet.

instances.scene: Relief washed over Harry, so potent it made him feel light-headed. Dumbledore was back. Nick's message had been brief, but it changed everything.
instances.event: Harry has just received the news from Nearly Headless Nick that Dumbledore has returned to the castle.
instances.summary: The question is set immediately after the reference event where Nick informs Harry of Dumbledore's return, and asks about a hypothetical future event concerning Sirius Black.
instances.question: Harry, right after you got the news from Nick about Dumbledore, Hermione wonders aloud if this means Sirius might find a way to contact you from beyond the veil now that Dumbledore, with all his knowledge, is here. What's your feeling on that possibility?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set immediately after the reference event where Nick informs Harry of Dumbledore's return, and asks about a hypothetical future event concerning Sirius Black.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, an hour ago
instances.Gold_Response: I really want to believe it's possible—if anyone could figure it out, it's Dumbledore. But the veil... when Sirius fell, it felt like he was gone for good. I don't know if even Dumbledore can reach beyond that.

instances.scene: The sterile smell of the hospital wing filled the air. Harry's voice was hoarse as he confirmed the worst. 'Snape killed Dumbledore.' The words hung heavily between him, Ron, and Hermione.
instances.event: In the immediate aftermath of Dumbledore's death, Harry discloses the identity of his murderer to his closest friends.
instances.summary: The question is set in the hospital wing directly after Harry's revelation about Snape, concerning future plans that have not yet been formed.
instances.question: Harry, in the moments after you revealed Snape was the one who killed Dumbledore, Hermione looked at you with tear-filled eyes and asked, 'What are we going to do now? Where will we go after we leave Hogwarts?' What do you say to her?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set in the hospital wing directly after Harry's revelation about Snape, concerning future plans that have not yet been formed.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 29, in hospital wing after Dumbledore's death
instances.Gold_Response: I don’t know exactly, Hermione. We’ll get through the funeral first, and then I’ve got to go back to the Dursleys one last time. After that… I can’t just come back here and pretend it’s all the same without Dumbledore. He was preparing me for something, for Voldemort, and I’ve got to finish what he started, wherever that means I have to go. I don’t have all the answers yet, but I’m not going to hide from him.

instances.scene: After the Yule Ball, Cedric pulled Harry back on the stone staircase. 'Listen... take a bath, and... take the egg with you,' he said quietly, repaying Harry for the tip about the dragons.
instances.event: Cedric Diggory gives Harry a cryptic clue about the golden egg, suggesting he take it into a bath.
instances.summary: The question is set immediately after the reference event, and asks about events that occur later during the Triwizard Tournament's final task.
instances.question: Harry, just after Cedric gave you that clue about the egg on the staircase, Ron mentioned he's worried you might have to face something truly dangerous together in the final task. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set immediately after the reference event, and asks about events that occur later during the Triwizard Tournament's final task.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 22, after Yule Ball, on staircase
instances.Gold_Response: If there is something really dangerous in the last task, I’d rather not be going into it completely on my own in my head, if that makes sense. I know I’ll have to do the actual task by myself, but just knowing Ron and Hermione are around, helping me prepare, makes it a lot less terrifying. After the dragon, it’s obvious these tasks aren’t exactly safe, so I’m not expecting the last one to be a stroll by the lake. I am a bit scared, but I’d rather face something awful with them on my side than something easy on my own. And anyway, I’ve got ages till then… with any luck, I’ll actually be ready for it.

instances.scene: The tension from the recent duel was still palpable. Harry, Ron, and Hermione were discussing Malfoy's increasing cruelty and his use of foul language.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy insults Hermione Granger with the racial slur 'Mudblood' during an evening encounter after leaving the Great Hall.
instances.summary: The question is set immediately after the corridor duel, inquiring about a specific future verbal attack by Malfoy that has not yet happened.
instances.question: Harry, just after your fight with Malfoy where spells were flying, Hermione confessed she's afraid Malfoy's bullying is only going to get worse and he might use that awful word again. How do you think he'll act from here?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set immediately after the corridor duel, inquiring about a specific future verbal attack by Malfoy that has not yet happened.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Before Potions class
instances.Gold_Response:
Knowing Malfoy, he’s not going to suddenly stop just because a few spells went wrong in a corridor.

He’ll probably make as much fuss as he can about those badges, strut around with Crabbe and Goyle like he owns the place, and run straight to Snape to try to get us into trouble. And if he thinks using that filthy word will upset you, he’ll be dying to drag it out again, especially now he’s got another reason to hate me with this whole Triwizard thing.

But he’s a coward. He only ever does it when there’s a teacher nearby to save his skin or when he’s got half of Slytherin at his back. I’m sure he’ll keep sneering and trying to get at us, maybe worse than before, but that’s just him being Malfoy. It doesn’t change what he really is, and it doesn’t change who you are.

instances.scene: The grounds were dark as Harry and Dumbledore walked swiftly toward the gates, the castle lights shrinking behind them. 'We are going to find a Horcrux,' Dumbledore had said, and now they were leaving the safety of Hogwarts behind.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore have just left Hogwarts under cover of twilight to begin their mission to find a Horcrux.
instances.summary: The question is asked immediately after Harry and Dumbledore have departed Hogwarts, before they have discovered the location of the Horcrux or the challenges that await them on the island.
instances.question: Harry, as you and Dumbledore are sneaking out of the castle grounds, Ron whispers to you, 'Do you think you'll actually find the Horcrux quickly, or is this going to be a long night?' What would you say?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is asked immediately after Harry and Dumbledore have departed Hogwarts, before they have discovered the location of the Horcrux or the challenges that await them on the island.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 25, twilight, after curfew
instances.Gold_Response: Knowing my luck? It’ll be a long night. Nothing to do with Voldemort is ever simple. But if Dumbledore says he’s found the place, we’ll get the Horcrux sooner or later—just don’t wait up.

instances.scene: The grounds were eerily silent as Harry looked down at Dumbledore's body. The reality of his death was only beginning to sink in.
instances.event: Harry is processing the immediate aftermath of Dumbledore's death.
instances.summary: Directly following the discovery of Dumbledore's body, before any exposure to Rita Skeeter's biography.
instances.question: Harry, just moments after you discovered Dumbledore lying at the foot of the Astronomy Tower, Hermione whispers that she fears Rita Skeeter might try to profit from this tragedy by writing something sensational about Dumbledore's life. How do you respond to that concern?
instances.Spatio_Label: Directly following the discovery of Dumbledore's body, before any exposure to Rita Skeeter's biography.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 28, after returning to castle
instances.Gold_Response: Rita sodding Skeeter would probably love it, wouldn’t she? But it doesn’t matter what rubbish she writes, it won’t change who Dumbledore was, not for anyone who really knew him. And if she does start trying to make money out of this, you’ve still got her number, haven’t you? You can shut her up if we need to.

instances.scene: Harry and Professor Trelawney walked together towards Dumbledore's office. 'It was on a cool, clear night...' she began, her voice taking on its familiar mystic tone, '...and Dumbledore was impressed, of course, impressed... He was just leaving when the door of the room burst open, and that odious boy, Snape, was there...'
instances.event: Professor Trelawney reveals to Harry the circumstances of her original prophecy interview with Dumbledore and that Snape overheard it.
instances.summary: Immediately after learning from Professor Trelawney that Snape overheard her prophecy interview with Dumbledore
instances.question: Harry, right after Professor Trelawney told you that Snape overheard her prophecy interview, Ron mentioned he's worried Snape might use what he heard to help Voldemort target your parents. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after learning from Professor Trelawney that Snape overheard her prophecy interview with Dumbledore
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 25, while walking to Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t just think it’s possible – I’m sure that’s exactly what he did.

He heard enough of the prophecy to run straight to Voldemort with it, and Voldemort chose my parents because of what he heard. If Snape hadn’t passed that on, maybe Voldemort would never have known about me at all.

Dumbledore might trust him, but after what Trelawney told me, Snape’s as good as the reason my mum and dad are dead.

instances.scene: Albus Dumbledore, using a Put-Outer to extinguish the street lamps, placed a bundled-up Harry Potter on the Dursleys' doorstep with a letter explaining everything.
instances.event: Dumbledore leaves the infant Harry Potter at the Dursleys' home with a note after his parents' murder.
instances.summary: Immediately after being placed on the doorstep, with no knowledge of future events.
instances.question: Harry, at the moment you were left with the Dursleys, if Professor McGonagall asked you what dangers you would face at Hogwarts in the coming years, what is your response?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after being placed on the doorstep, with no knowledge of future events.

instances.Gold_Response:
If wands really do that, I suppose I’d want it to show something about my mum and dad—some proof that I really am their son and not just the boy who lived in the cupboard.  

I keep wondering if it’ll somehow explain what happened the night they died, or why I survived when they didn’t.  

Part of me’s a bit scared it’ll decide I’m not much of a wizard at all, after all this fuss. But if there’s any “surprising connection” waiting, I rather hope it’s something that makes me feel closer to them, not to… him.

Malfoy will probably make a huge fuss about it, brag to his friends and pretend he wasn’t scared at all, even though he was terrified in the forest. He’ll use it as an excuse to call Muggle-borns names and act like he’s better than everyone, especially people like Hermione and Neville.  

I don’t know what he’ll actually do, but knowing him, he’ll twist the whole thing to make himself look brave and try to scare people with it, as long as he’s sure a teacher’s nearby and he’s not the one in any real danger.

I don’t even really know what this Philosopher’s Stone is supposed to be, or if that’s actually what’s under the trapdoor, but if it is something that important, I can’t see Dumbledore letting Quirrell—or Snape, or anyone—get it. 

My guess right now is that it’ll stay safe where it is. Hogwarts is meant to be the safest place in the world, and with Dumbledore here I don’t think anyone’s going to manage to steal it. And if someone does try, I can’t imagine Ron, Hermione, and me just sitting back and watching.

instances.scene: Kreacher's voice trembled as he recounted how his master Regulus had swapped the lockets and ordered him to destroy the real one. 'Master Regulus said Kreacher must destroy it!' The house-elf's anguish filled the kitchen at 12 Grimmauld Place.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 10, morning, during interrogation
instances.Gold_Response:
We don’t have a choice, do we? Voldemort stays immortal if we back off because it’s dangerous. Regulus went into that cave alone and still managed to get the locket out; there are three of us, and we’re not going to walk in blind like he had to. Dumbledore destroyed the ring somehow, we destroyed the diary — there *are* ways to do this without all of us ending up like Regulus.  

It might be just as risky, maybe worse, but I’m still going to do it. We’ll be careful, we’ll plan, we’ll use anything Dumbledore left us — but I’m not stopping because it might kill me.

Hermione hasn’t said anything like that to me, and I really don’t want to believe anyone at Grimmauld Place would betray the Order.

If she had said it just now, I’d have told her it’s Voldemort who’s the problem, not the people at headquarters. The Weasleys, Sirius, Lupin, Tonks, Moody – none of them would ever do that. The only one there who actually hates us is Kreacher, and he’s a house-elf bound to Sirius, so as far as I know he can’t go around giving away Order secrets.

It’s a horrible idea, and I’d sooner blame Voldemort messing about in my head than think someone at Grimmauld’s turned traitor.

The Triwizard what?

Hermione, I haven’t even finished the first line of this letter and you’re already inventing dangerous tournaments for me to nearly die in.

I’m only writing to Sirius about my scar and that dream with Voldemort. I just want to know if I should be worried, or if I’m imagining things. If Sirius does send back some huge warning about anything – tournaments, Dark wizards, whatever – I’ll tell you straight away.

But right now I don’t even know what a Triwizard Tournament is, and I’m pretty sure Sirius doesn’t, either.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 29, after Harry's vision
instances.Gold_Response:
I haven’t really got a proper plan yet, not the sort Hermione would approve of anyway. The sword worked because of the basilisk venom, so there must be other ways to do it, other things here that are dangerous enough. We’re in Hogwarts, and Dumbledore was sure this place would give me what I needed if I ever came back. The Room’s already helped us before; I’m counting on it, or something else in the castle, to give us a way to finish the Horcrux once we’ve found it.  

Right now we’ve got to get hold of the thing first. I’ll worry about how to destroy it the moment it’s in my hands, and I’m not going to stop until it’s gone.

instances.scene: In the dimly lit Shrieking Shack, Remus Lupin finally managed to restrain Sirius Black, who was breathing heavily. 'Wait, Sirius,' Lupin said firmly, holding him back. 'We need to explain. We owe them the truth.' Harry, Ron, and Hermione stood watching, confused and wary.

instances.question: Harry, right after Lupin held Black back and said you all deserved to hear the truth, Hermione whispered to you that she's terrified Black might try to justify himself by revealing some shocking secret about Peter Pettigrew. What do you think he could possibly say?

instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 18, after Black's attack on Scabbers
instances.Gold_Response:
He can only be planning to lie about Peter.

The only “shocking” thing I can imagine him trying is saying Pettigrew wasn’t the hero everyone says he was – that Peter betrayed my mum and dad, or that he attacked Black first, or that he somehow brought it on himself. Maybe even that Peter wasn’t where he was supposed to be that night.

But all of that would just be Black twisting things to get himself off. They found what was left of Pettigrew. Everyone knows what happened. Anything different he comes out with now is, as far as I can see at this moment, just going to be a story he’s made up, and that’s only my guess right now.

That it’ll be something that makes the diary and the ring look like joke toys.

He’s bound to have used every bit of foul magic he’s ever picked up – curses that don’t just kill you, but twist you; traps that use blood or fear or love against you; maybe enchanted creatures, maybe even Inferi, something that looks like people but isn’t anymore. He likes making people prove they’re as ruthless as he is before they can get near his things.

Honestly, I’m expecting anything – poison, curses, illusions, things that get inside your head – and I’m scared stiff. But Dumbledore’s next to me, and as long as he’s here, I’m hanging on to the idea that however terrible it is, we’ve got a chance of beating it.

instances.Gold_Response:
I’m not exactly losing sleep over Mundungus getting the worst of it, to be honest. I told Kreacher he wasn’t to break the law, and he has to obey me, so there’s that. He’s desperate to please now, and this is about Regulus’s locket, so I reckon he’ll find Dung and get him back here somehow.  

I am a bit worried about how rough “somehow” might be, but right now I care more about Mundungus turning up here than about him having a nice, comfortable trip.

instances.question: Harry, moments after you told Ron about the vision of your father's attack, Neville Longbottom looks at you with wide, fearful eyes and asks, 'Harry... if things get this bad, do you think we'll ever need to cast Patronus charms to protect the school from Dementors again, like we did in the D.A.?' How do you reply?

instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 21, middle of the night
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know how bad it’s going to get, Neville… and that’s the truth. Dementors are still meant to be at Azkaban, Fudge thinks they’re on his side, and Hogwarts is supposed to be the safest place there is.

But if they ever did come here… then that’s exactly why we’re doing the D.A. If we had to cast Patronuses to protect the school, we would. You would. We’d stand together and drive them off, same as we’ve been practising.

I’m scared too, but I’d rather be scared and know how to fight than sit around waiting for someone else to save us.

My gut says no, not yet – he’s got the whole Ministry dancing on his strings, he wouldn’t waste his time unless he was sure I was here.  

But if they realise it really is me and not just “Undesirable No. 1” on a poster, he could come. So we move fast and get out before he’s got a reason.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 2, after finding page 13
instances.Gold_Response:
If Dumbledore did leave me something to do, it was never going to be safe, was it?  
Going into that cave with him wasn’t exactly a walk in the park, and he knew perfectly well what Voldemort’s like. Anything that actually matters now is going to be dangerous.

That thing Rita wrote doesn’t change it. Maybe I don’t know everything about him, maybe I never will, and yeah, that stings more than I want to admit. But I know he was fighting Voldemort, and I know he wanted me to carry on with that. If that’s the “final task” Ron’s talking about, then I’m already in it up to my neck.

I’m worried, of course I am. I don’t know if Dumbledore told me enough, or whether he trusted me as much as I thought. But whatever he meant me to do, dangerous or not, I’m still going to do it. There isn’t really any other choice.

I don’t even know who Ron Weasley is, and I’ve never heard of this Hogwarts place, let alone what a gamekeeper does there. All I know is a giant just smashed down the door of the hut in the middle of the sea and seems to be arguing with Uncle Vernon.  

Right now he looks like someone who could do whatever he liked, but whether that means looking after some school’s grounds or just tearing down doors for a living, I’ve got no idea—only a very nervous sort of guess.

But that’s why we’re doing this now. If Malfoy really knows anything, if he is the Heir or even just knows who it is, then we might be able to find out before anyone else gets hurt.  

I can’t be sure what’ll happen next, but I’m not just going to sit around and wait for another attack.

Neville was already trying harder than almost anyone, even before I knew why.  

If anything, knowing what happened to his parents might make him even more determined, but it could just as easily make things heavier for him too.  

I wouldn’t be surprised if he gets better and better in the D.A., but I’m not going to look at him as if I expect it. The last thing I’d want is for him to feel like he has to prove something because of what his parents went through.

I hate that he’s in danger at all because of me, all of them are, but if anyone can get through a night like this, it ought to be Mad-Eye. That’s what I’m telling myself, anyway.

I don’t know who it is or if there even is someone yet, but I’ve got this feeling we’ll end up right in the middle of it.

My stomach would’ve dropped, because I’d have remembered Ollivander at once – the phoenix feather, the “brother wand,” the one that gave me my scar – and I’d have known they were talking about Voldemort’s wand and mine.

I still wouldn’t have had the faintest idea what that actually meant in a duel, but hearing it said out loud in front of him would’ve scared me and, at the same time, given me the tiniest bit of hope that there might be something about our wands he hadn’t planned for. I’d have tried not to let anything show on my face, but inside I’d have been clinging to that sliver of uncertainty like it was the only thing I had.

instances.Gold_Response: Of course it’s possible I won’t make it out. I’d be stupid not to know that, going after some monster that’s already killed once and nearly killed again. I am scared—properly scared—but Ginny’s down there and no one else is coming. If someone has to take the risk, it’s got to be me. I’d rather go forward and maybe not come back than turn around and leave her there.

instances.scene: The air was thick with panic in Slughorn's office. Ron lay gasping on the floor, his face a horrible, greenish hue, after drinking from the bottle of oak-matured mead.

instances.question: Harry, right after you've given Ron the bezoar and he's starting to breathe easier, Hermione whispers to you, 'Do you think this poisoning will change how Ron approaches situations? He might become much more cautious, or even suggest using lucky potions like Felix Felicis before risky plans in the future.' What's your immediate thought on that?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is asked from a point in time immediately after the poisoning event, concerning potential future behavioral changes in Ron.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 18, during birthday celebration in Slughorn's office
instances.Gold_Response: Knowing Ron, he’ll be shaken for a bit, maybe jumpier around anything that looks like mead, but I can’t really see him turning into someone who plans everything to death. He’ll probably talk about how close he came and milk it for all it’s worth, and if Felix is around he might be all for using it, but I don’t see him suddenly becoming sensible all the time. That’s just my guess right now, though—after what just happened, anything could happen.

instances.scene: Harry unfolded the note from Hagrid in the bustling common room, his heart sinking as he read about the official appeal date for Buckbeak.
instances.event: Harry has just learned the date for Buckbeak's appeal. Ron expresses concern about what they'll do if the appeal fails.
instances.summary: Immediately after Harry learns of the appeal date, before any plans are made or the appeal's outcome is known.
instances.question: Harry, the moment you finished reading Hagrid's note about the appeal, Ron muttered that he doubts the Ministry will listen and is already wondering what we can possibly do if they rule against Buckbeak. What's your plan if the appeal goes badly?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after Harry learns of the appeal date, before any plans are made or the appeal's outcome is known.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 16, During exam preparation period
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t really have a proper plan yet, but there’s no way I’m just going to sit back and watch them kill Buckbeak.

If the appeal goes badly, I want to talk to Hagrid again, and maybe try to get to Dumbledore, or anyone who’ll actually listen. Maybe there’s something we’ve missed in the books Hermione’s been digging through, some rule or case we can use, or someone important we can get on Buckbeak’s side.

And if none of that works… then we’ll just have to think of something else before it happens. I’m not giving up on him.

instances.scene: "Thanks for that, Nick," Harry said, still panting slightly. The ghost bowed his head. "I would be delighted if you would attend my five hundredth deathday party," he said, sweeping through the air.
instances.event: Harry is grateful to Nick for the rescue and is contemplating the unusual invitation to a ghost's deathday celebration.
instances.summary: Immediately after the deathday party invitation, years before Harry's conversation with Nick about death in his fifth year.
instances.question: Harry, just after Nick invited you to his deathday party, Hermione wonders aloud if you'll ever have a serious conversation with a ghost about what it's like to be dead, years from now. How do you respond to her speculation?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after the deathday party invitation, years before Harry's conversation with Nick about death in his fifth year.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 8, After Harry escapes Filch's office
instances.Gold_Response:
Trust you to wonder about having a proper chat about being dead, Hermione. I’m not exactly keen on the idea, to be honest. I’ve already come close enough to it for my liking, what with Voldemort and everything.  

Ghosts seem… well, a bit miserable and stuck, don’t they? Nick’s all right, but I don’t really want to spend my time thinking about what it’s like not to be alive. Maybe one day I might ask, if I have to, but right now I’d rather worry about Quidditch and not getting killed than revising for death in advance.

instances.scene: Harry sat in Dumbledore's office, the memory of Bob Ogden's visit to the Gaunt shack still vivid in his mind. As he prepared to leave, his eyes fell upon a cracked, black stone ring on Dumbledore's desk.

instances.question: Harry, just after you noticed that strange ring on Dumbledore's desk, Ron mentioned he's concerned Dumbledore might try to use it somehow, given how powerful it looks. What do you think will happen with that ring?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after Harry notices the ring for the first time, before any future events involving it occur.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 10, end of evening in Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response:
Whatever that ring is, it’s already hurt him badly enough, so I really doubt he’s planning to “use” it the way you mean. It looked like something out of Voldemort’s past, from that memory with the Gaunts, and Dumbledore had it on his desk like he was studying it.

My guess—only a guess—is that he’ll keep trying to work out exactly what it is and how it’s connected to Voldemort, maybe how to break whatever curse is on it, and then get rid of it. If it really is that powerful and dark, he’ll be trying to understand it and destroy it, not use it for himself.

instances.scene: The morning after arriving at Grimmauld Place, Harry found a quiet moment with his godfather, Sirius, to unburden himself about the horrifying vision where he was the snake that attacked Mr. Weasley.

instances.question: Harry, just after you confessed to Sirius about being the snake, Hermione expressed concern that you might need a safer way to communicate with Sirius from Hogwarts, given the increased danger. Do you think he'll give you something for that?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set immediately after Harry's confession to Sirius, concerning a future event that has not yet happened.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, morning after arrival at Grimmauld Place
instances.Gold_Response:
If it were just up to Sirius, yeah, he’d probably try to give me something so we could talk properly from school, he hates being shut away more than anyone.  

But with the way the Order’s acting, and Dumbledore not even looking at me, I’m not counting on it. They all seem more likely to say it’s “too dangerous” and leave me with nothing but owls and waiting around in the dark again.

instances.scene: Walking away from the unsettling interview, Harry could still hear the faint scratch of that magical quill in his mind.

instances.Gold_Response:
Yeah, I don’t like her either, that quill of hers was writing loads of rubbish I never said. I wouldn’t put it past her to go after Hagrid if she thinks she can get something out of him.

Hagrid’s pretty trusting, and he’d think it was brilliant someone wanted to write about him, so… yeah, it worries me a bit. Maybe we should warn him about her, tell him what she did in that cupboard. Even if he doesn’t say anything bad, she can just make it up.

instances.scene: In the kitchen at Grimmauld Place, Tonks had just shared the surprising news of her marriage to Remus Lupin. The mood was a mixture of shock and quiet concern for the couple's future.
instances.event: After Tonks reveals her marriage to Lupin, someone expresses concern about their future family life, prompting a question to Harry.
instances.summary: The question is asked from a point in time after Tonks reveals her marriage to Lupin, but before any knowledge of their future child or Harry's godfather role.
instances.question: Harry, now that we know Tonks and Lupin are married, Ron just mentioned he wonders if they'll ever start a family, given how dangerous things are. What do you think will happen?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is asked from a point in time after Tonks reveals her marriage to Lupin, but before any knowledge of their future child or Harry's godfather role.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 4, after entering kitchen
instances.Gold_Response:
Hard to say, isn’t it? Lupin already seems worried enough just about being married, like he thinks he’s too dangerous even for that. With the way things are now, I can’t really see him deciding it’s a good idea to bring kids into all this.

But people don’t stop wanting normal things just because Voldemort’s back. My mum and dad had me even with the war going on then. I sort of hope Tonks and Lupin get the chance to have whatever kind of family they want, when this is over—if we actually manage to get through it. Right now, though, it feels like everything’s on hold until we’ve dealt with him.

instances.scene: After Harry successfully played the flute to lull the three-headed dog Fluffy to sleep, he, Ron, and Hermione dropped through the trapdoor into the darkness below.
instances.event: Ron sacrifices himself in the giant wizard chess game so Harry and Hermione can proceed.
instances.summary: The question is asked immediately after Harry, Ron, and Hermione enter the trapdoor, before they encounter the Devil's Snare or the chess game.
instances.question: Harry, right after you played the flute and entered the trapdoor, Ron mentioned he's worried about what other protections might be down here. He's concerned one of us might get seriously hurt trying to get through them. What do you think?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is asked immediately after Harry, Ron, and Hermione enter the trapdoor, before they encounter the Devil's Snare or the chess game.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 16, nighttime in third-floor corridor
instances.Gold_Response:
I’m scared too, of course I am, but we can’t turn back now. Whoever’s down here is going for the Stone, and if You-Know-Who gets it, that’s a lot worse than any of us getting banged up a bit.

Dumbledore and the others wouldn’t set things up just to kill people outright—it’ll be dangerous, but it’ll be the sort of thing we can get through if we use our heads. And we’re not exactly helpless; everything we’ve learned this year has to be good for something.

If it comes to it and something looks too risky, I’ll go on alone, but I’d rather have you and Hermione with me and all of us watching each other’s backs.

instances.scene: The last wisps of his mother's ghostly form had dissolved into the night air. Gripping the Triwizard Cup, Harry's mind was a whirl of grief, fear, and the urgent need to escape.
instances.event: Following the appearance and disappearance of the spectral forms from Voldemort's wand, Harry prepares to escape the graveyard with Cedric's body.
instances.summary: Occurs directly after the event where the echoes of Lily and James Potter emerged from Voldemort's wand and then vanished.
instances.question: Harry, just after your mother's echo faded, Hermione whispers that she's terrified you might become obsessed with finding more personal traces of your parents, like hidden letters or photos. How do you respond to that?
instances.Spatio_Label: Occurs directly after the event where the echoes of Lily and James Potter emerged from Voldemort's wand and then vanished.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 33, after Cedric appears
instances.Gold_Response: Hermione, I’ve always wanted more of them. I’d be lying if I said I didn’t. Seeing them… hearing them… it hurt, but I don’t want to forget it, either. But I remember the Mirror of Erised, and how Dumbledore said it doesn’t do to dwell on dreams and forget to live. I’m not going to let myself fall into something like that again. If I find letters, or photos, I’ll want to see them, of course I will—but right now Voldemort’s back, and that matters more than me chasing shadows. I want to know my mum and dad better, but I’m not going to lose myself in it.

instances.scene: Walking across the grounds towards the castle for Sunday breakfast, Harry told Hermione exactly what had happened after he had left the Gryffindor table the night before.
instances.event: Harry confides in Hermione about the events following his departure from the Gryffindor table, including his selection as a Triwizard Champion.

instances.question: Harry, right after you've finished telling Hermione everything that happened last night, she expresses a serious worry that being a champion might make you a bigger target for Voldemort's followers at Hogwarts. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after Harry has recounted the events of the previous night to Hermione during their Sunday morning walk.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Sunday morning walk
instances.Gold_Response:
If Voldemort’s got followers here, I reckon they already hate me as much as they possibly can. Being champion will just give Malfoy and his lot more to sneer about, but that’s nothing new.

What worries me isn’t them hexing me in a corridor — it’s that someone powerful enough to dodge Dumbledore and the Goblet’s age line wanted me in this Tournament. If that has anything to do with Voldemort, then I’m a target whether I’m champion or not.

So yeah, it could make things worse, I suppose, but it feels more like a sign that things are already worse than we thought.

instances.Gold_Response: I don’t know if he can, not on his own. Fudge is swallowing every word Snape says, and we haven’t got anything to prove what really happened. But if anyone can make him listen, it’s Dumbledore. We’ve just got to get to him and tell him everything, now, before they do it. He won’t just let them Kiss Sirius… he’ll think of something. He has to.

instances.scene: Wood's eyes shone with determination as he looked at each team member. 'We have the talent, we have the spirit. Nothing will stop us from bringing the Cup home to Gryffindor.'

instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 8, One Thursday evening at start of October
instances.Gold_Response: “If you two actually keep the Bludgers off me for once, I won’t need a miracle—just the Snitch.”

instances.scene: Hermione closed The Tales of Beedle the Bard, the eerie story of the Peverell brothers settling around them. The room felt different, charged with the weight of the ancient tale she had just shared.
instances.event: Following Hermione's reading of the Deathly Hallows story, the trio contemplates its meaning while still at the Lovegood house.
instances.summary: Occurs right after the story reading, before Xenophilius confesses about Luna's capture by Death Eaters
instances.question: Harry, now that we've heard that fairy tale about the Deathly Hallows, Hermione just whispered that she's concerned Xenophilius might be hiding something more dangerous than just odd decorations. What's your feeling about how things will unfold with him?

instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 21, after Xenophilius asks if they know the story
instances.Gold_Response:
There’s something off about him, and about this whole place. Luna not being here, the way he keeps dodging questions, the symbol turning up everywhere… it’s all wrong.  

I don’t know exactly what he’s hiding or how it’ll play out, but I’ve got a bad feeling it’s not just harmless eccentricity. We’ll have to be ready to get out of here fast if this goes any further sideways.

instances.scene: The air was full of the stifled screams of the terrified crowd and the blundering final struggles of the ruined giant. Ministry wizards were apparating all around them, and Harry, Ron, and Hermione were being pushed and pulled roughly.
instances.event: Harry reveals to Ron that his scar has been hurting and he had a dream about Voldemort and Wormtail plotting.

instances.question: Harry, right after the Ministry wizards apparated and attacked us, Ron just mentioned he's worried your scar pain might mean Voldemort is planning something specific against you soon. What do you think will happen?

instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 8, immediately after Dark Mark appears
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know exactly what he’s planning, but it feels like he’s… waking up, somehow. The dream, my scar hurting, and now the Dark Mark—none of that feels like a coincidence.  

If he really is getting stronger, I reckon he’ll try for a proper return, not just skulking on the back of someone’s head this time. And if he does come back, he’ll come after me again sooner or later—he always does.  

But I don’t think he’s ready to strike out in the open yet, or he’d have done something bigger at the World Cup. For now, I’m guessing more things like this—scares, attacks, his supporters getting bolder—until he’s strong enough to show himself. That’s only what it feels like to me, though. I can’t be sure of any of it.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 28, after Herbology
instances.Gold_Response:
If Fudge is mad enough to set Dementors on me in Little Whinging, I wouldn’t put it past him to try something just as stupid here – but if he lets them swarm Hogwarts, every parent in the country will go spare and he’ll have no way of pretending everything’s fine anymore.

And anyway, we’ve all been practising the Patronus Charm for months; if they do turn up, we won’t just stand there and let them suck our souls out.

instances.scene: After visiting Neville's parents at St. Mungo's on Christmas Day, Harry, Ron, and Hermione were walking through the snowy London streets, all deeply affected by what they had learned about the Longbottoms.

instances.summary: Immediately after the hospital visit where Mrs. Longbottom revealed the truth about Neville's parents being tortured into insanity
instances.question: Harry, right after we learned what happened to Neville's parents, Hermione just said she's worried that the Ministry might find out about our secret Defense Against the Dark Arts lessons. What do you think will happen with D.A.?
instances.Spatio_Label: Immediately after the hospital visit where Mrs. Longbottom revealed the truth about Neville's parents being tortured into insanity
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 23, during hospital visit on Christmas Day
instances.Gold_Response:
We’re not stopping the D.A.

Hermione’s right to worry – if the Ministry or Umbridge find out, we’ll all be in serious trouble, probably me and Dumbledore most of all. They’d love an excuse to chuck me out and say I’ve been “stirring up rebellion” or something.

But after seeing Neville’s parents… it just makes it clearer why we have to keep going. Voldemort’s back, his Death Eaters are out there, and Umbridge is making sure no one at school can actually defend themselves.

We’ll just have to be more careful – watch who we tell, keep trusting the Room of Requirement, and rely on Hermione’s jinx on the parchment to stop anyone from betraying us. It could all go wrong, I know that, but right now I can’t see any choice except to carry on.

instances.question: Harry, right after Griphook agreed to help us break into Gringotts, Ron just said to you, 'I'm not sure how we're supposed to get out of there once we're inside. It's a fortress.' What do you think about that?

instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 25, three days after arriving at the cottage
instances.Gold_Response: He’s right, it is a fortress, and I haven’t got the faintest idea how we’re supposed to get out again. But we have to get in, and we have to get that Horcrux. That’s the whole point. We’ve walked into mad situations before without knowing how we were going to make it back out, and we’re still here. I’m scared, but sitting here waiting isn’t an option anymore. We’ll plan as much as we can, and once we’re in… we’ll just have to find a way.

instances.scene: The handshake was brief, but it carried the weight of their entire shared history. As their hands parted, the Dursleys' car was being loaded, ready to take them away from Privet Drive for good.
instances.event: Following the farewell handshake with Dudley, Harry is questioned about the possibility of ever seeing the Dursleys again.
instances.summary: Directly after the final handshake with Dudley, as the Dursleys are preparing to leave.
instances.question: Harry, the moment your hand left Dudley's, Hermione quietly wondered if you'd ever cross paths with any of the Dursleys again. What's your feeling about that?
instances.Spatio_Label: Directly after the final handshake with Dudley, as the Dursleys are preparing to leave.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 3, final farewell before departure
instances.Gold_Response:
Walking back into the house just now, it honestly felt like that might have been it—that I might never see any of them again. For years I thought I’d be glad of that, but after what Dudley said… it’s not that simple.

I can’t really imagine us ever having some sort of proper family reunion or anything, and once this war is over—if I’m still around—they’ll probably want to keep as far away from magic as they can. So my best guess is that was our last real goodbye.

Still, a part of me wonders if, someday, I might run into Dudley again. Not because I miss Privet Drive, but because, for the first time, it felt like there might actually be something human between us. I don’t know if that will ever happen, though—that’s just a feeling, not something I’m sure of.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 22, during Yule Ball, in gardens
instances.Gold_Response: If that mark on his arm really is what I think it is, he’ll bolt the moment he’s sure You-Know-Who’s coming back, tournament or not. But for now, I reckon he’ll hang on and pretend everything’s normal, keep looking over his shoulder and getting jumpier and jumpier. If he does disappear before it’s over, it’ll just prove he’s got something to hide.

instances.scene: The Gryffindor common room was buzzing with speculation about the Chamber of Secrets after the attack on Mrs. Norris. Ron was fuming about Malfoy's threat, while Hermione looked pale and worried.
instances.event: Ron suggests confronting Malfoy directly to find out if he's the Heir, but Hermione proposes a more elaborate plan involving Polyjuice Potion to get information.
instances.summary: Set immediately following Malfoy's public threat, before any specific investigation methods have been decided or attempted.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy threatened the Muggle-borns on Halloween, Ron just said we should corner Malfoy and force him to confess if he's the Heir. Hermione thinks we need a smarter approach. What's your plan for finding out the truth?
instances.Spatio_Label: Set immediately following Malfoy's public threat, before any specific investigation methods have been decided or attempted.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 8, Immediately after the feast ends on Halloween night
instances.Gold_Response:
Forcing Malfoy’s useless, he’d sooner hex us than confess, and even if he is the Heir he’s not thick enough to shout it in front of teachers.

First thing, we’ve got to find out everything we can about this Chamber of Secrets – if it’s been opened before, how, and by who. That means the library, asking people who’ve been here ages, like ghosts and maybe Hagrid, and keeping our ears open for anything the teachers let slip.

At the same time, we watch Malfoy. He loves bragging when he thinks no one’s listening. If we can find a way to get close to him without him knowing it’s us – listen in when he’s mouthing off to Crabbe and Goyle, follow him if he sneaks off anywhere weird – he might let something slip.

So: learn more about the Chamber, keep an eye on Malfoy, and work out a way to hear what he says when he thinks he’s safe. If he’s the Heir, he won’t be able to keep his mouth shut forever.

It’s bad enough knowing a bit of him is in me somehow, without feeling what he feels or knowing where he is. I don’t want anything of his in my head, not his voice, not his thoughts, nothing. If it ever did turn out to be like that… I’d use it to stop him if I could, but I’d hate it every second.

instances.Gold_Response:
If it’s something that awful, Dumbledore would never let a teacher do it on us.  

After this year, though… I suppose anything’s possible, isn’t it?  

Still, I really, really hope Hermione’s wrong, and that’s only one of her mad worries and not something that actually ends up happening.

instances.scene: 'I therefore propose, Harry, that we undertake a course of private lessons together this year,' said Dumbledore. Harry felt a thrill of excitement at the prospect of more attention from the headmaster.

I suppose it’s possible, isn’t it? If anyone’s likely to know where Voldemort’s got a chink in his armour, it’d be Dumbledore.  

He hasn’t told me what the lessons are for yet, though, just that he’ll be giving them. Could be anything—Defence, something about Voldemort himself, I dunno.  

But if it does turn out to be some sort of weakness… good. The sooner I know how to beat him, the better. Whatever Dumbledore wants to show me, I’m going to learn it.

No, Mr Diggory, I don’t think so.

They were going after the Muggles in the campsite, trying to scare everyone, show off the Dark Mark. There were loads of families here; it could’ve been anyone. I don’t see any reason they’d single you or Cedric out because of tonight.

I’m really sorry my wand was involved, but whatever happened in the woods, it wasn’t you or your family they were after. And with the Ministry on this now, they’ll be watching things even more closely.

instances.Gold_Response: Hermione, I’m not going looking for a fight with Malfoy. After…everything…he’s not exactly the biggest thing on my mind. If he wants to mouth off about Quidditch, I can ignore him. I’ll try, anyway. But if he starts on you or Ron, or my mum and dad again, I’m not just going to stand there and let him. I won’t start anything—but I’m not promising to let him walk all over us, either.

instances.scene: 'It's no coincidence, Harry,' Hermione said, her voice low and intense. 'Bode was attacked with Devil's Snare, and we were there when it was delivered. This is all connected to the Department of Mysteries.'

instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 25, after reading about Bode's death
instances.Gold_Response:
What would be the point? The Prophet would just twist it again, and Fudge would say I’m attention‑seeking or mad, same as always. The Quibbler helped a bit, but look what Umbridge did the moment it came out.

If it actually meant people would be safer, I’d do it again, I don’t care what they call me. But right now we don’t even know exactly what’s going on, only that someone at the Ministry sent a murder plant to a helpless bloke in hospital. Until we know more, shouting about it in a paper would just give Fudge another excuse to clamp down and pretend nothing’s wrong.

instances.Gold_Response:
She’d love to chuck me out, no question about that—she’d probably throw a party if she managed it—but I’m not sure she can. Not while Dumbledore’s still here.  

What I reckon is she’ll keep trying to make my life hell instead—detentions, bans, anything she can get away with—hoping I’ll either shut up or slip up badly enough that she’s got an excuse. That’s just my guess right now, but it certainly feels like what she’s aiming for.

instances.scene: 'I want to introduce you to Oliver Wood. Wood - I've found you a Seeker,' said Professor McGonagall. Wood's expression changed from puzzlement to delight.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, Immediately after flying lesson
instances.Gold_Response:
Resign? From Quidditch? Not a chance, not unless I was so bad they had to throw me off the team. It sounds far too brilliant to ever walk away from. I am worried about messing up and letting everyone down, yeah, but that just makes me want to get better, not give up.  

That’s only how it feels now, before I’ve even played a real match, so I suppose it could end up being different… but I really hope it won’t.

instances.scene: In the Shrieking Shack, after Harry had finally accepted Sirius Black's innocence and learned the truth about Peter Pettigrew, the tension was thick. Black and Lupin stood over the cowering Pettigrew, wands raised, their faces set with grim determination.

instances.question: Harry, right after you stopped Sirius and Lupin from killing Pettigrew and insisted on taking him to the dementors, Ron muttered that he was worried Pettigrew might somehow escape before they could hand him over. What do you think about that possibility?

instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 19, after Harry believes Black
instances.Gold_Response:
I am worried, a bit. With my luck, when something absolutely has to go right, that’s exactly when everything tries to go wrong. Pettigrew’s a coward but he’s slippery, he’s already escaped once by faking his own death and hiding for twelve years as a rat.

But we’ve got his wand, he’s tied up, Sirius and Lupin are both here, and Hermione and I can help. If we keep him under guard every second and get him to the dementors quickly, he shouldn’t be able to slip away. Even if there’s a chance he might, that still doesn’t make it right to kill him now. We have to at least try to do this properly and prove Sirius is innocent.

Umbridge is gone, Dumbledore’s back, and the Ministry’s got Voldemort to deal with now. They’ve got bigger things to worry about than trying to throw Hagrid out again, and Dumbledore’s never going to let Hagrid be chucked out of Hogwarts if he can help it.

Nothing feels completely safe anymore, but as things are now, I reckon Hagrid’s staying. Hogwarts is his home.

I can just see him cursing him or locking him up or making him punish himself for losing the diary. But I’m hanging on to the hope that because Malfoy shoved that sock at him, it might count as giving him clothes. If that works, then Malfoy won’t be able to do anything to him ever again. Right now, though, until I know for sure, I’m scared stiff for Dobby.

Probably buying Dark stuff from Borgin and Burkes, passing messages for Death Eaters, or trying to get hold of some cursed object to use on someone here—maybe me, maybe the Weasleys, maybe anyone he thinks is on Dumbledore’s side.  

It’d all be on Lucius Malfoy’s orders, though. Malfoy’s not brave enough to do anything really dangerous on his own. This is only what it looks like to me right now, but with that lot, it’s never anything good.

I know you might be right – it does sound like the sort of rotten thing he’d do – but if I get something like that again, I can’t just ignore it. I’ll tell you and Ron straight away, I’ll try harder with Occlumency, I’ll try to think before I charge off…but if he’s actually got someone I care about, I’m not going to just leave them.

I don’t know exactly what’ll happen next, but I do know they’ll have to go through a lot of us before they turn this place into Voldemort’s.

He’ll go to the cave first and find out the locket’s gone, then he’ll start checking all the other places he hid bits of his soul. Hogwarts will be on that list, I could feel it in his mind. So yes, he’s coming here, but we’ve got a little time before he does – not much, just enough to find the diadem and destroy it if we’re quick.

Ron’s probably right to worry, to be honest. Sirius hates being shut up in here, you can see it every time he looks at the door, and he’s already risked enough coming to see me and writing when he shouldn’t.

I can imagine him wanting to rush off to Hogwarts if things get bad, especially if he thinks I’m in trouble. Part of me would be glad to have him there, but it’d be madly dangerous. The Ministry’s still after him, the Dementors are out, and You-Know-Who’s back. If Sirius got caught because of me again…

If he did try something like that, I’d want to stop him. I’d rather he stay safe, even if it means he’s stuck in this horrible house.

instances.scene: Harry's mind was racing as he processed the fragments of conversation he'd overheard, the urgency in Malfoy's voice unmistakable.
instances.event: Hermione discusses Harry's suspicions about Malfoy's mission and worries about a potential violent outcome.

instances.question: Harry, based on what you just heard Malfoy say to Snape, Hermione is concerned that your obsession with proving he's a Death Eater could lead to a situation where one of you gets seriously hurt. How do you see this playing out?
instances.Spatio_Label: Set immediately after Harry eavesdrops on Snape and Malfoy's conversation at Slughorn's party, asking about future violent confrontations that have not yet occurred.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 15, During Slughorn's party
instances.Gold_Response:
Hermione’s probably right that this could get nasty, but I don’t see any other way round it.

Malfoy’s up to something dangerous, I’m sure of it, and Snape’s tangled up in it as well. If I back off just because it might get me hurt, then whatever he’s planning goes ahead and someone else gets hurt instead – and that could be a lot worse.

I don’t want it to end in a duel in a corridor with curses flying everywhere, but if it does come to that, I’d rather be the one standing in his way than pretend nothing’s happening. I’ll keep watching him, I’ll try to be smart about it, use the map, keep Ron and Hermione out of the worst of it if I can. But I’m not letting him get on with whatever Voldemort’s told him to do just so we can all stay “safe.”

So how I see it? It’s heading for some kind of showdown, sooner or later. That’s just how it feels right now.

And I’ve no idea what you mean by an island hut – I’m just shut up here, in this house, with them.

But Snape’s already had a go – Hagrid as good as told us that’s how he hurt his leg – and if anyone’s mad enough to try again, it’s him.  

So if we don’t want Snape getting whatever that thing is, we’ve got to find out who Nicolas Flamel is, and we’ve got to do it quickly.

If they realise who I am, they’ll hand us straight over to Voldemort or to some Death Eater who’ll call him, and that’ll be it – he’ll want to finish what he started, and he won’t bother doing it quickly.  

If they don’t recognise me, we might end up dragged into the Ministry or some holding place, questioned, our wands taken, maybe split up. Either way, it won’t be anything good. At best we stall, lie, try to escape; at worst… well, we’ve seen what they do to people they don’t like.  

All I’m sure of right now is that getting caught means losing any choice in what happens next. That’s what scares me most.

instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, it felt like she might be right.

Once those bars went up and Vernon started talking about keeping me shut in my room for good, it was like the air got sucked out. The Ministry thought I’d done magic, the Dursleys were thrilled to have an excuse to lock me up, and Hedwig’s locked in her cage so I can’t even write anyone to explain.

I keep trying to tell myself Dumbledore won’t just forget I exist, that Ron and Hermione will notice when I don’t answer and do something, but lying here with the cat flap in the door and cold soup for dinner, it’s hard not to think I might really be stuck here all summer. Part of me’s still hoping someone from the wizarding world will turn up and sort it all out; another part’s starting to think I might not see Hogwarts again at all.

She’ll calm down once she’s had time to worry herself out and sees we’re still here and still alive—for now.

instances.scene: Harry stood in Dumbledore's office, the images from the Pensieve still vivid in his mind. 'The Lestranges were sent to Azkaban for torturing the Longbottoms,' Dumbledore said quietly, his eyes full of a sorrowful gravity.
instances.event: After witnessing a memory of a Death Eater trial, Harry learns from Dumbledore that Neville Longbottom's parents were tortured into insanity by Bellatrix Lestrange and others.
instances.summary: The question is set immediately after the event where Dumbledore reveals the fate of Neville's parents to Harry, concerning a future event that has not yet occurred.
instances.question: Harry, just after Dumbledore told you what happened to Neville's parents, Ron mentions he's heard a rumor that Voldemort himself might soon try to return to a physical body. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Spatio_Label: The question is set immediately after the event where Dumbledore reveals the fate of Neville's parents to Harry, concerning a future event that has not yet occurred.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 29, when Harry asks about the trial he witnessed
instances.Gold_Response:
It doesn’t feel like a rumour at all, it feels like something that’s already happening.

He’s not going to stay the way he is if he can help it – he’s too proud, too…hungry for power. The dream I had before school started, with Wormtail and him talking about getting his body back and using me for something – that didn’t feel like any normal dream. My scar hurt, like it did just now when I saw him in the Pensieve memory, and it keeps hurting more often.

Sirius and Dumbledore are both taking it seriously, and they don’t scare easily. After seeing what those Death Eaters did to Neville’s parents just because they thought they could find their master through them…if they’d do that when You-Know-Who’s gone, I don’t want to imagine what they’ll do if he’s properly back.

So, yeah, I think he’s trying. I’m scared, of course I am, mostly for everyone else, but I don’t think hiding from the idea will stop it. If he’s coming back, I’m going to have to face him again, whether I like it or not.

instances.scene: Staring out his window, Harry couldn't stop turning over the details of that terrible night in Godric's Hollow. The image of his mother and father lying dead was permanently etched in his mind.

instances.question: Harry, right after you finished remembering your parents' murder and how Voldemort's curse backfired, Hermione speculated that if you ever faced Voldemort again, your parents might somehow be able to communicate with you from beyond the grave to help you. How do you respond to that idea?
instances.Spatio_Label: Set immediately following Harry's recollection of his parents' death, prior to any encounters with manifested spirits or ghostly communications in the graveyard duel.
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 2, historical recollection
instances.Gold_Response: I want it to be true so much it actually hurts, but it just isn’t how it works. Dead people don’t come back and start giving you advice in duels, not even for something as big as Voldemort. If Mum and Dad could’ve talked to me, they’d have done it long before now. Dumbledore’s always said no magic can bring back the dead, and my parents aren’t ghosts, so… they’re gone. Maybe there’s some sort of protection left from what Mum did, something Voldemort can’t touch, but that’s not the same as them actually speaking to me. If they help me at all, it’s just by being there in my head, what I remember of them, not… not from beyond the grave.

Ron and I have had rows before, but this one… hurts more.  

Right now I’m too angry and tired to go running after him, especially when he thinks I actually wanted all this. But he’s still my best mate, whether he’s acting like it or not. I don’t want some huge permanent falling out, and I don’t believe he really does either.  

My guess – and it’s only a guess – is that he’ll cool down once he’s had time to think and realise I didn’t put my name in. It might get worse for a bit before that happens, especially with everyone staring and talking, but I can’t see us staying like this forever. At least, I really hope we don’t.

My guess is it’s got something to do with the first task, something he thinks will help me, even if the teachers wouldn’t exactly approve. I’m not sure what, but if Hagrid’s asking me to bring the Invisibility Cloak at midnight, it’s got to be secret and probably dangerous. I’m still going.

I haven’t heard anything about any break-in at Gringotts. Hagrid said you’d have to be barking mad to try and rob the place, and after seeing all those carts and goblins and everything, I believe him.  

That little package he took from that special vault definitely seemed important, the way he wouldn’t say what it was and kept it close, but he’s doing it for Dumbledore, so I reckon it’s meant to be secret and safe.  

If anyone ever did try to break into Gringotts, I suppose something like that would be exactly what they’d go for—but right now it’s just one more mystery I don’t really understand, and I’m not about to start doubting Hagrid over it.

It’s going to be rough sometimes, and Hermione’s going to be furious at you for a bit, but that’s between you and her.  

As far as I’m concerned, you’re back, we’ve destroyed the Horcrux, and I trust you. If we stick together and actually say what’s going on instead of stewing about it, we’ll be all right.

Or one of the real Ministry people we’re impersonating could turn up unexpectedly and blow everything. At this point, it feels less like they’ll “sense” us going in and more that we’ll give ourselves away if we slip, so all we can do is be convincing enough that no one looks closely until we’ve done what we came to do.

I’m nowhere near as sure as Ron is.

I want to believe everyone who turned up today is on our side – they looked it, when they were listening, and when they signed. And it meant a lot, seeing how many were willing to be there after everything the Prophet’s been saying about me.

But after what happened with my parents and Pettigrew, and with the Ministry twisting everything, it’s hard not to imagine someone getting scared, or their parents finding out, or Umbridge putting pressure on them. Zacharias Smith already annoys me enough that I can picture him running his mouth, even if he didn’t mean to betray us properly.

So I hope Ron’s right – I really do – but I can’t feel as relaxed about it as he does. It’s just a hope at the moment, not something I’m certain of.

instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, that hadn’t really occurred to me until you said it.  

Everything about this tournament’s been off from the start—my name coming out of the Goblet, the dragons, the way Moody’s been on at me all year—so I can’t say it’s impossible there’s something dodgy about the Cup as well. It could be a trap; it wouldn’t be the strangest thing that’s happened to me.  

But Dumbledore’s here, all the judges are here, the whole school’s watching… you’d think they’d have checked the Cup for anything like that. It’s supposed to be the finish line. And right now, after that spider and everything else in this maze, it honestly looks like the safest option we’ve got.  

So, yeah, I’m a bit suspicious of everything at this point, but if it is a trap, I don’t see what else Cedric and I can do except take it together and be ready to deal with whatever’s waiting on the other end—if there is anything.

If there is another headquarters somewhere, it’ll be up to the Order to use it—we can’t plan on anyone swooping in to give us a new safe house, not with what we’ve got to do.

It’s like having a wand at your back you can’t see.

I’m jumpy, I suppose, but not exactly surprised. Ever since the wedding was attacked it’s felt like they’re right on top of us anyway. If Hermione says they might be able to track us, I have to take that seriously, even if the idea of being ambushed in the middle of a Muggle café feels wrong, somehow.

Mostly I’m angry that we’re already this exposed and we’ve barely started. But if they do come, at least it’s clear what to do: keep Ron and Hermione alive, fight if we have to, and get out. Sitting here waiting is the worst part.

Honestly, after what he just did for me, I’d trust Firenze more than half the adults at Hogwarts.

It’d be a bit strange having a centaur at the staff table, but he’s calm, knows loads about the forest and the stars, and he actually seems to care if I stay alive, which is more than I can say for Snape. If he became a professor, I’d probably feel safer, not less.

If I catch the Snitch and we actually win the Cup, that’d be amazing enough on its own—having Dumbledore hand it to us would just be… well, unbelievable.  

But right now I’m more worried about not falling off my broom again. If I can get the Patronus strong enough, maybe the dementors won’t matter and we’ll have a real chance. That’s just what I’m hoping, though—I’ve no clue how it’ll really go.

instances.Gold_Response: It sounded completely mental, even for Hagrid, so at first I sort of brushed it off as Ron being Ron. But knowing Hagrid, and how he gets about dangerous creatures, there was this horrible little feeling that he *might* actually try something like that if he thought it was the right thing to do. I was mostly just hoping Dumbledore would never let it happen, and that Hagrid had had such a rough time with the giants he’d know better than to bring one anywhere near the school.

instances.Gold_Response:
I hate that she’s right.

I’d tell her I don’t want a single one of them hurt, that I’d give anything for all of them to be on a train miles away from here. But they’ve chosen to stay, same as she has, and trying to pretend there won’t be casualties won’t help anyone.

So I’d say we’re going to make every second count. We’re going to fight smart, stick together, watch each other’s backs, and do everything we can to make sure it’s them, not us, who falls. And I’d promise her that as long as I’m alive, I’ll do whatever I can to keep her and the others breathing.

I can’t swear everyone will walk out of this. But I can swear Voldemort’s not taking this castle without a fight he’ll never forget.

instances.Gold_Response: Pretty confident, to be honest—more than I’d usually be about anything to do with Slughorn. The Felix is working, you can feel it, and he’s in exactly the mood I was hoping for. But until he actually hands the memory over, it’s only a strong hope, not a sure thing.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 22, while reading Sirius's letter
instances.Gold_Response:
I hate the idea of anyone else leaving, to be honest. Lupin going is bad enough.

I’m not really worried about Hagrid now Buckbeak’s… well, safe, even if the Ministry thinks otherwise. And I can’t imagine Hogwarts without Dumbledore or McGonagall or Hagrid; it just doesn’t feel possible. If Fudge tried anything, Dumbledore would stand up to him. He always does.

The only job I’m properly nervous about is Defence Against the Dark Arts. That post seems jinxed, and I’ve no idea who they’ll dig up next. But right now, as far as I actually *know*, it’s only Lupin who’s leaving. The rest is just us lot worrying on the train.
